record_scope_reconstruction: Adré road crossing from Chad into West Darfur, Sudan. The 2024 humanitarian permission regime and the WFP food-truck operational return are distinct phases at the same named route. Neither covers all traffic or all agencies, and exceptional March/April aid prevents a continuous zero-aid interval.

source_checks.finding: Original operational overview PDF text inspected, p.3: February 21 note withdrew prior Chad-to-Sudan authorization; March 13 limited permission for sixty Adré trucks; August 16 new three-month authorization. No exact exhaustion date of earlier exception or border-control coordinates.
Full primary August 16 statement identifies Adré Chad-to-Darfur route and welcomes authorization; supplies are ready to move, so it is permission rather than observation of first convoy.

Full relevant original operational statement inspected: August 21 publication dates WFP food trucks crossing Tuesday evening, August20. It separately acknowledges March and April WFP convoys during official closure; no all-agency or final-delivery inference.

Indexed Adré coordinate is explicitly a city/place node, not the border control. Rejected as a crossing coordinate. Unsourced travel-site coordinates and generic town proximity do not establish the humanitarian route facility.

phase_decisions.phase_applicability: Modal scope: single_site. Chad-to-Darfur humanitarian permit regime, February 21 through August 15–16 authorization, with March/April exceptions. Hold exact geography because named Adré control point has not been independently located; no whole Sudan–Chad frontier substitute.
unresolved: Source-backed coordinate of Adré aid-truck border facility unresolved.
Permission and physical control are distinct; no universal or continuous traffic stoppage.
